rows.patient_note: A 65-year-old male with a history of hypertension and diabetes presents with altered mental status and jaundice. He reports feeling progressively weak over the past week with associated abdominal discomfort and swelling in his lower extremities. On examination, he is lethargic with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 10, and scleral icterus is noted. His vital signs reveal a heart rate of 90 beats per minute. Laboratory investigations reveal a serum creatinine level of 92.12 µmol/L and a total bilirubin level of 1.57 mg/L, suggesting mild renal impairment and cholestasis, respectively. Additionally, his platelet count is decreased at 88400/µL. There are signs of overt hypotension, and so the patient is receiving norepi and epi infusions at 0.1 mcg/kg/min each, with a concurrent dopamine infusion at 6.32 mcg/kg/min. The patient is currently receiving 41 % FiO₂ with continuous positive airway pressure. His partial pressure of oxygen is recorded to be 90 mm Hg. Notably, there is no urine output recorded. Given the constellation of symptoms and laboratory findings, further investigation into the etiology of his hepatic and renal dysfunction is warranted.

mdcalc_rules: Use worst value over 24 h. Resp PaO2/FiO2: >=400 0; 300-399 +1; 200-299 +2; <=199 and not mechanically ventilated (CPAP counts as ventilated) +2; 100-199 ventilated +3; <100 ventilated +4. Platelets x10^3/uL: >=150 0; 100-149 +1; 50-99 +2; 20-49 +3; <20 +4. GCS: 15 0; 13-14 +1; 10-12 +2; 6-9 +3; <6 +4. Bilirubin mg/dL (umol/L): <1.2 (<20) 0; 1.2-1.9 (20-32) +1; 2.0-5.9 (33-101) +2; 6.0-11.9 (102-204) +3; >=12 (>204) +4. CV (mcg/kg/min): no hypotension 0; MAP <70 +1; dopamine <=5 or any dobutamine +2; dopamine >5 or epi <=0.1 or norepi <=0.1 +3; dopamine >15 or epi >0.1 or norepi >0.1 +4. Renal creatinine mg/dL (umol/L): <1.2 (<110) 0; 1.2-1.9 (110-170) +1; 2.0-3.4 (171-299) +2; 3.5-4.9 (300-440) or UO <500 mL/day +3; >=5.0 (>440) or UO <200 mL/day +4.
